entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 136:1-26 . The theme is the same as that of Psalm 135. God should be praised for His works of creation and providence, His deliverance and care of His people, and judgments on their enemies, and His goodness to all. The chorus to every verse is in terms of that of Ps 106:1; 118:1-4 , and was perhaps used as the Amen by the people, in worship (compare 1Ch 16:36; Ps 105:45 ).

entries.heading: 5, 6. by wisdom
entries.text: 5, 6. by wisdom --or, "in wisdom" ( Ps 104:24 ). made --literally, "maker of." above the waters --or, "higher than the waters" ( Ps 24:2 ).

entries.heading: 15. overthrew
entries.text: 15. overthrew --literally, "shook off," as in Ex 14:27 , as a contemptuous rejection of a reptile.

entries.heading: 23. remembered us
entries.text: 23. remembered us --or, "for us" ( Ps 132:1 ). our low estate --that is, captivity.

entries.heading: 24. And hath redeemed us
entries.text: 24. And hath redeemed us --or, literally, "snatched us"--alluding to the sudden deliverance effected by the overthrow of Babylon.
25. To the special favors to His people is added the record of God's goodness to all His creatures (compare Mt 6:30 ).

entries.heading: 26. God of heaven
entries.text: 26. God of heaven --occurs but once ( Jon 1:9 ) before the captivity. It is used by the later writers as specially distinguishing God from idols.
